records.title: Humanity From One Original Human and Mate

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: STRONG CREATION PARALLEL WITH DIFFERENCES IN DETAIL

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Common origin and mate parallel Genesis; Quran 4:1 does not name Adam/Eve or mention rib/serpent/deception. Pending NT comparison includes 1 Tim 2:14 and 2 Cor 11:3.

records.title: Polygyny and Marriage Structure

fields.label: Comparison evidence
fields.value: Genesis 2; OT polygyny; Matthew 19; Pastoral Epistles

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Quran explicitly codifies up to four wives under justice condition; biblical corpus contains polygyny but later Christian marriage teaching requires canonical development analysis.

records.title: Female Inheritance Rights and Sex-Differentiated Succession

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both recognize structured inheritance and female rights in defined circumstances, but formulas differ.

records.title: Incest and Forbidden-Kin Marriage Laws

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both prohibit close-kin unions with overlapping but not identical lists.

records.title: Slavery Regulation

fields.label: Comparison evidence
fields.value: Torah slavery/captivity laws; NT slavery texts

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: SHARED ANCIENT INSTITUTION / MAJOR LEGAL-ETHICAL COMPARISON REQUIRED

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both corpora operate in slaveholding societies; compare permission, regulation, sexual access, manumission, and later trajectories without pretending regulation equals abolition.

records.title: Marital Authority and Physical Discipline

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: PARTIAL STRUCTURAL PARALLEL + SIGNIFICANT LEGAL/ETHICAL DIFFERENCE

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both contain asymmetrical household structures; NT marital instruction does not plainly contain a matching husband-administered physical-discipline sequence.

records.title: Intentional Versus Accidental Homicide

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: STRONG LEGAL PARALLEL WITH DIFFERENT PROCEDURES

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both sharply distinguish accidental killing and murder.

records.title: Abraham as Friend of God

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Abraham is explicitly described as God’s friend/intimate in both traditions.

records.title: Marital Breakdown and Reconciliation

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: PARTIAL ETHICAL PARALLEL / SIGNIFICANT PROCEDURAL DIFFERENCE

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Both value reconciliation; Quran gives asymmetrical spouse-specific procedures not directly paralleled in NT marital discipline.

records.title: The Crucifixion of Jesus

fields.label: Comparison evidence
fields.value: Canonical Gospels; Pauline letters; early Christian and Roman evidence

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Quran explicitly denies killing/crucifixion; earliest Christian evidence and ordinary historical scholarship strongly support Jesus’ crucifixion under Pontius Pilate. Pre-Islamic substitution/docetic traditions existed but do not independently verify Quranic denial.

records.title: Origin/Purpose of Jewish Dietary Restrictions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Quran frames some restrictions as punishment for wrongdoing; Torah presents dietary law within holiness/covenant legislation. Full corpus and Jewish chronology layers required.

records.title: Trinity / “Three”

fields.label: Comparison evidence
fields.value: Matthew 28:19; Pauline triadic formulas; Nicene-Constantinopolitan tradition

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: SUBSTANTIVE THEOLOGICAL CONTRADICTION; REPRESENTATION ACCURACY OPEN

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Quran rejects “Three” while Christianity affirms one God in Father/Son/Spirit. Whether Quran accurately targets Nicene doctrine remains under the Christology flag.

records.title: Quranic Representation of Christian Triadic Belief

fields.label: Comparison evidence
fields.value: Nicene Christianity: Father, Son, Holy Spirit; Mary not divine

fields.label: Classification
fields.value: SUBSTANTIVE THEOLOGICAL CONTRADICTION + SERIOUS REPRESENTATION QUESTION

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: Quran clearly rejects Trinity/divine Christology, while 5:116 raises a separate historical question about whether Christian belief is represented accurately, especially regarding Mary.

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP01 vv001-028
paragraphs: Surah tag: Medinan by the traditional list
Why this cut: Creation, orphans, marriage cap, first inheritance table, sexual misconduct, forbidden degrees. 4:29 opens commercial devouring.

People: fear your Lord who created you from one nafs and created from it its mate and spread from them many men and women. Fear God in whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Give orphans their property; do not exchange the bad for the good; do not consume their property into your property. If you fear you will not be just toward the orphans, marry what is pleasing to you of women — two, three, and four. If you fear you will not be just, then one, or those your right hands possess. That is nearer that you not incline. Give women their ṣaduqāt as a gift; if they remit any of it to you with pleasure, consume it wholesome. Do not give the safīh their property which God made a standing for you; feed and clothe them from it and speak to them a known-good word. Test the orphans until they reach marriage; if you perceive in them rushd, hand them their property. Do not consume it in extravagance and haste before they grow. Whoever is rich should abstain; whoever is poor may eat with maʿrūf. When you hand it over, have witnesses. Men have a share of what parents and nearest leave, and women have a share, little or much, a prescribed share. When kin and orphans and the poor are present at the division, provide for them from it and speak a known-good word. Those who, if they left weak offspring, would fear for them: let them fear God. Those who consume orphans’ property unjustly consume fire into their bellies. God instructs you concerning your children: for the male the like of the portion of two females. If there are women above two, for them two-thirds; if one, half. For parents, each a sixth if there is a child; if no child and parents inherit, the mother has a third; if there are siblings, the mother a sixth — after a bequest or debt. You do not know which of parents and children is nearer in benefit. For you half of what your wives leave if they have no child; if they have a child, a quarter — after bequest or debt. For them a quarter if you have no child; if you have a child, an eighth. If a man or woman is inherited kalāla and has a brother or sister, each a sixth; if more than that, they share a third — after bequest or debt, without harm. Those are God’s ḥudūd. Whoever obeys God and His messenger He admits to Gardens; whoever disobeys and transgresses the ḥudūd He admits to the Fire. Those of your women who commit the indecency: four witnesses from you; confine them in the houses until death takes them or God makes a way. The two who commit it among you: harm them; if they repent and put things right, leave them. Repentance is for those who do evil in ignorance then repent soon. Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death is present, they say I repent now, nor for those who die as kāfirūn. It is not lawful to inherit women against their will, nor to hem them in to take part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear indecency. Live with them with maʿrūf. If you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God has put much good in it. If you want to replace a wife with another and you have given one of them a qinṭār, do not take anything from it. How can you take it after intimacy and they have taken from you a firm covenant? Do not marry women whom your fathers married, except what has already passed; it was an indecency, hateful, and an evil way. Forbidden to you: your mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brother’s daughters, sister’s daughters, milk-mothers, milk-sisters, wives’ mothers, step-daughters in your guardianship from wives you have gone into — if you have not gone into them there is no blame — wives of your sons from your loins, and that you gather two sisters, except what has passed. And the muḥṣanāt of the women except those your right hands possess. The Book of God upon you. Lawful beyond that is that you seek with your property, muḥṣinīn not musāfiḥīn. What you enjoy of them: give them their wages as an obligation. Whoever of you cannot afford to marry believing muḥṣanāt: from those your right hands possess of your believing slave-girls. God knows your faith; you are of one another. Marry them with their people’s permission and give them their wages with maʿrūf, muḥṣanāt not musāfiḥāt and not taking lovers. If they are married and then commit an indecency, on them half of what is on the muḥṣanāt of punishment. That is for those who fear hardship among you; that you endure is better. God wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you. God wants to turn to you; those who follow desires want you to incline a great incline. God wants to lighten for you; the human was created weak.

Created you from one soul; from it its mate; from them many men and women. Fear God and the wombs. QB-0082: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gen 1–2 / 5:2 (one human, male and female). The Quran does not here name Eve or the rib. Wombs as a parallel object of fear next to God is this verse’s own.

Give them their property; no swap of bad for good; no folding their wealth into yours. Test until nikāḥ-age; if rushd appears, hand it over with witnesses. Rich guardian abstains; poor may eat with maʿrūf. Unjust consumption is fire in the belly — same image as 2:174. This is the orphan-protection spine of the surah’s name.

If you fear you will not be just toward the orphans, marry what pleases you of women — mathnā wa-thulātha wa-rubāʿ. If you fear you will not be just: one, or those your right hands possess. Nearer that you not ʿūl.

Asbāb (ʿĀʾisha): about marrying orphan wards for their property. Level 1 also functions as a numerical cap at four plus a justice-condition that points back to one. Mā malakat aymānukum is named as the alternative-to-four. This packet describes the sentence. It does not unpack slave-concubinage as a how-to.

QB-0083: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that multiple-wife households exist in the HB (Abraham, Jacob, David, Solomon) with no four-cap. ADDITION of an explicit ceiling and a justice-or-one clause. NT trajectory is toward one-man-one-woman in the pastorals (1 Tim 3:2). Three different architectures again.

Women have a prescribed share — a reversal of a reported jāhiliyya default that cut daughters and minors out (TAFSIR for the default; Level 1 is that women have a share). Male child = two female shares. Daughters only: two-thirds if two or more; half if one. Parents: sixths when there is a child; mother a third if no child and no siblings; sixth if siblings. Husband: half / quarter. Wives: quarter / eighth. Kalāla sibling line: sixth each or a third to share. After bequest and debt, without ḍirār.

2:180’s bequest-for-parents-and-kin now has to live next to these farāʾiḍ. Later uṣūl often treats 4:11–12 as limiting 2:180. That is a naskh claim (Level 4). Level 1: both passages exist; 4:11–12 are called farīḍatan min Allāh and ḥudūd.

QB-0084: CONTRAST with Torah inheritance, which is son-centered (Deut 21:15–17 double portion for the firstborn son; Num 27 daughters inherit only if no son, then marry inside the tribe). The Quran gives daughters a standing share even when sons exist (half a brother’s share), and gives the widow and the widower named fractions. Different math, not a copy.

Women who commit the fāḥisha: four witnesses; confine in houses until death or God makes a way. The two who commit it: harm them; if they repent and repair, leave them. 24:2 will later name a hundred lashes. Relation of 4:15 house-confinement to 24:2 is a classic naskh debate. Do not import 24:2 yet as if 4:15 were already cancelled. Tawba: for ignorance-then-soon-return, not for deathbed or for dying in kufr.

Unlawful to inherit women against their will or to hem them in to claw back dower, unless a clear fāḥisha. Live with them with maʿrūf. Dislike may hide good. Replacing a wife: even a qinṭār already given is not to be taken back after intimacy and a firm covenant. This is an anti-inheritance-of-widows and anti-clawback panel.

Fathers’ wives (except what passed). Then the list: mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts both ways, nieces both ways, milk-mother, milk-sister, wife’s mother, step-daughters under guardianship if the marriage was consummated, sons’ wives from the loins, two sisters at once. Muḥṣanāt forbidden except those the right hand possesses. Book of God upon you. Beyond that: seek with property, chaste not unchaste. Wages for what you enjoy are an obligation.

QB-0085: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 18’s incest table (mother, sister, aunt, daughter-in-law, two sisters in Lev 18:18). ADDITION of milk-kinship as a marriage-bar. Lev 18:18 is “not a wife to her sister as a rival while she lives”; 4:23 is “that you gather two sisters.” Same object, slightly different wording. “Except those your right hands possess” after the muḥṣanāt ban is the verse’s own exception; later fiqh loads it. Level 1 records the exception-clause without turning this packet into a slavery manual.

Who cannot afford believing muḥṣanāt: believing slave-girls with their people’s permission, wages with maʿrūf, chaste. After nikāḥ, if they commit fāḥisha: half the punishment of the free muḥṣanāt. Endurance is better. God wants to make clear, to guide to the ways of those before you, to turn to you, to lighten — the human was created weak.
“Ways of those before you” is an explicit continuity claim for this family-law panel (QRQ-0007 / 0003).
Each parent if there is a child
Mother if no child, no siblings
Sixth each; third to share if more
OT polygyny uncapped; NT pastorals monogamy-leaning; this verse caps and conditions
Daughters and widows as fixed heirs
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 18; ADDITION of milk-kin
Created from one nafs; fear God and the wombs
Orphan property; test for rushd; fire-eaters
Marry two three four if just; else one or those the right hand possesses
Women have a prescribed share; farida table of 4:11–12
Indecency: four witnesses and confinement; tawba window
Women not inherited against will; no clawback of a qintar after intimacy
Forbidden degrees including milk-kin; two sisters; except right-hand possess
Believing slave-girls if one cannot afford free muḥṣanat; man created weak

Al-Nisāʾ opens by tying fear of God to the wombs and then legislating property, marriage numbers, and fractions. Daughters and widows are given named shares. The four-cap is a ceiling with a justice-brake, not a command to reach four. Lev 18 is the closest Bible table; Num 27 is the closest inheritance analogue and it is not the same math.
Next: 4:29–43 (do not consume property by bāṭil; kill not; if you fear you will not be just among wives you will not be able; prayer when drunk later to be tightened; tayammum).

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP02 vv029-043
paragraphs: O believers, do not consume your property among yourselves by bāṭil, except it be trade by mutual consent. Do not kill yourselves; God is merciful to you. Whoever does that in ʿudwān and ẓulm We shall roast in a Fire. If you avoid the great sins you are forbidden, We will cover your misdeeds and admit you at an honorable entry. Do not wish for that by which God has favored some of you over others. For men a share of what they earned; for women a share of what they earned. Ask God of His bounty. To everyone We have appointed heirs of what parents and nearest leave. Those with whom your right hands have made a compact: give them their share. Men are qawwāmūn over women with what God has favored some of them over others and with what they spend of their property. Ṣāliḥāt are devoutly obedient, guarding the unseen as God has guarded. Those whose nushūz you fear: admonish them, shun them in the beds, and iḍribūhunna. If they obey you, do not seek a way against them. If you fear a split between the two, send an arbiter from his people and an arbiter from her people. If they want to repair, God will reconcile them. Worship God and associate nothing with Him. Iḥsān to parents, to kin, orphans, the poor, the neighbor who is near, the neighbor who is far, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those your right hands possess. God does not love who is proud, boastful — who are stingy and command people stinginess and hide what God has given them. Those who spend their property to be seen of people and do not believe in God and the Last Day. Satan is their companion. What harm would it do them if they believed and spent of what God provided? God does not wrong even the weight of an atom; if it is a good He multiplies it. How will it be when We bring from every ummah a witness and We bring you as a witness against these? Those who disbelieved and barred from God’s way have gone far astray. Those who disbelieved and did ẓulm: God is not about to forgive them or guide them except the path of Jahannam. O people, the messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord; believe; it is better for you. If you disbelieve, to God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. O believers, do not approach prayer while you are sukārā until you know what you are saying, nor junub except passing through, until you wash. If you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands. God is ever pardoning, forgiving.
4:29–31 property; do not kill yourselves; kabāʾir

Property: no bāṭil consumption except tijāra by mutual consent. Lā taqtulū anfusakum — do not kill yourselves / one another (both hearings live). Aggression and ẓulm → Fire. Avoid the kabāʾir you are forbidden and smaller deeds are covered. This is not a list of the kabāʾir; it is a covering-promise if they are avoided.

Do not wish what God used to favor some over others. Men have a share of what they earned; women have a share of what they earned. Ask God of His bounty. Heirs appointed for what parents and kin leave. Those your right hands contracted: give them their share. 4:32 is often read against envying the 4:11 male-double share; Level 1 is earned-share plus a ban on wishing the other’s favor. Compact-heirs interact with later ʿaqd / walāʾ law (Level 4).

Al-rijālu qawwāmūna ʿalā l-nisāʾi bi-mā faḍḍala llāhu baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍin wa-bi-mā anfaqū. Ṣāliḥāt: qānitāt, guarding the unseen as God guarded. Those whose nushūz you fear: ʿiẓūhunna, wahjurūhunna fī l-maḍājiʿ, wa-ḍribūhunna. If they obey you, do not seek a way against them. If you fear a split: an arbiter from his people and from hers; if they want iṣlāḥ God will reconcile.
Level 1: a maintenance-and-favor basis for qiwāma; a three-step response to feared nushūz; a hard stop if obedience returns; a two-family arbitration if a split is feared.

Ḍaraba in Arabic has a wide range (strike, set forth, turn away, separate). Classical tafsīr majority heard a constrained strike. Some modern readings hear separation / departure. This packet records the range. It does not treat the verse as a license-manual. 4:19 (live with them bi-l-maʿrūf) and 4:35 (arbiters) sit in the same surah.

QB-0086: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with household-authority language in the HB and NT (Gen 3:16; Eph 5:22–33; 1 Pet 3:1–7). DIFFERENCE: Eph 5 frames husband-headship inside Christ’s self-giving; 4:34 frames qiwāma inside favor-and-spending and names a nushūz sequence. Neither text is the other text.
4:36–42 iḥsān list; atom-weight; you as witness

Worship God; no shirk. Iḥsān to parents, kin, orphans, poor, near neighbor, far neighbor, companion at your side, traveler, those the right hand possesses. God does not love the proud who are stingy and command stinginess and hide God’s gift, nor those who spend to be seen and do not believe. Satan is their qarīn. God does not wrong an atom; good is multiplied. The addressee is brought as a witness against “these.” Those who disbelieved and did ẓulm: not forgiven, not guided except the path of Jahannam. The messenger has come with truth; believe; if you disbelieve, the heavens are still God’s.

Do not approach ṣalāh while sukārā until you know what you are saying. Do not approach junub except passing through, until you wash. Ill, journey, privy, or lāmastumu l-nisāʾ, and no water: seek ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban and wipe faces and hands.

Wine path in this project: 2:219 (sin greater than benefit) → 4:43 (do not pray drunk) → 5:90 (avoid). 4:43 is the middle step, not the final ban. Lāmastum: “touch” vs “sexual contact” is a live fiqh split; both hearings exist. Tayammum is dry substitute when water is missing or unusable.

QB-0087: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that cult requires sobriety and purity (Lev 10:9 priests not to drink when entering the tent; 1 Cor 11 unworthiness at the table). Tayammum as earth-wipe has no exact Torah twin.
rising against / marital recalcitrance — sense argued
strike / separate / set forth — range live
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with household-order texts; different framing from Eph 5
No prayer while drunk; purity; earth-wipe
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on sober cult; tayammum is ADDITION
No batil consumption except consented trade; do not kill yourselves
Avoid kabair and lesser deeds are covered; do not wish another's favor; earned shares
Men qawwamun; three-step nushuz; two arbiters if split feared
Ihsan list including neighbors and right-hand possess; atom-weight justice
Messenger as witness; believe he has come with truth
No salah while drunk or junub; tayammum when no water

Trade by consent; no self-killing; kabāʾir covering; earned shares for men and women. 4:34–35 is the household-authority panel: qiwāma tied to favor and spending, a three-step nushūz sequence whose third verb is argued, then two-family arbitration. Wine is not yet 5:90; it is already barred from prayer. Earth stands in for water.
Next: 4:44–70 (those given a portion of the Book, magic slander already met at 2:102, obey God and the messenger, if you differ take it to God and the messenger).

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP03 vv044-070
paragraphs: Have you not seen those given a portion of the Book buying error and wanting you to err from the way? God knows your enemies. Among the Jews are those who alter words from their places and say we hear and we disobey, hear as one not heard, rāʿinā — twisting their tongues and slandering the dīn. If they had said we hear and we obey, hear, and unẓurnā it would have been better. God has cursed them for their kufr; they do not believe except a little. O you given the Book, believe in what We sent down confirming what is with you, before We wipe faces and turn them on their backs or curse them as We cursed the sabbath-people. God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him; He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Whoever associates with God has invented a tremendous sin. Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? God purifies whom He wills. Look how they invent the lie against God. Have you not seen those given a portion of the Book who believe in jibt and ṭāghūt and say of those who disbelieve these are better guided than those who believe? Those are the ones God has cursed. Or have they a share of the kingdom? Then they would not give people a naqīr. Or do they envy people for what God gave them of His bounty? We gave the house of Abraham the Book and ḥikmah and We gave them a great kingdom. Among them is one who believed in it and among them is one who turned from it. Those who disbelieve Our signs We shall roast in a Fire; whenever their skins are done We replace them with other skins. Those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt We shall admit to Gardens. God commands you to render trusts to their owners and when you judge between people to judge with justice. O believers, obey God and obey the messenger and those in authority among you. If you dispute in anything, refer it to God and the messenger if you believe in God and the Last Day. Have you not seen those who claim to believe in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you, wanting to take judgment to ṭāghūt though they were commanded to reject it? When it is said come to what God sent down and to the messenger, you see the hypocrites turning from you. How is it when a disaster hits them for what their hands sent ahead they come to you swearing by God we meant only iḥsān and tawfīq? Those — God knows what is in their hearts. So turn from them, admonish them, say to them about themselves penetrating words. We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by God’s leave. If, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked God’s forgiveness and the messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found God relenting, merciful. No, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge in what they differ in, then find in themselves no tightness from what you decided, and submit a full submission. If We had written on them kill yourselves or go out from your homes they would not have done it except a few. Whoever obeys God and the messenger — those are with those God has favored: the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the shuhadāʾ, and the ṣāliḥīn. Excellent companions. That is bounty from God.
4:44–46 portion of the Book; hear and disobey; raʿina

Again a portion (naṣīb) of the Book, not the whole named as discarded. Altering words from their places; hear and disobey (the 2:93 formula); rāʿinā as a twisted address. Unẓurnā would have been better. Cursed for kufr; they believe only a little. QCA tahrīf here is displacement of words plus tongue-twist, same file as 2:75 / 3:78.
4:47 confirm what is with you; sabbath-curse memory

Believe in what We sent down confirming what is with you — before faces are wiped and turned back or a curse like the sabbath-people. The prior book is still “what is with you,” invoked as something this sending confirms. Sabbath-curse points at 2:65 / 7:163 without retelling the fish-story here.
4:48 shirk not forgiven; less than that for whom He wills

Inna llāha lā yaghfiru an yushraka bihi wa-yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li-man yashāʾ. Associating is a tremendous invented sin. 4:116 will repeat the same sentence. This is the Quran’s sharpest interior ranking of sin so far: shirk is the unforgiven meeting-condition; what is less than it is forgiveable for whom God wills. How that lives next to 4:31’s covering of lesser deeds if kabāʾir are avoided is a ranking question, not a merge. 4:17–18 already limited tawba at death and at dying-in-kufr.

QB-0088: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with first-commandment gravity (Exod 20:3–5; “I am a jealous God”). DIFFERENCE: the NT’s unforgivable-sin file is blasphemy against the Spirit (Mark 3:29), not this shirk formula. Do not equate the two unforgivables.
4:51–54 jibt and ṭāghūt; envy of Abraham’s house

A portion of the Book who believe in jibt and ṭāghūt and rank the disbelievers as better guided. Cursed. No share of mulk — they would not give a naqīr. Envy of what God gave people of bounty. We gave Āl Ibrāhīm the Book, ḥikmah, and a great kingdom. Among them who believed and who turned away. Jibt/ṭāghūt: idols, soothsayers, illegitimate powers — sense-range is real; Level 1 is illicit allegiance plus a ranking insult aimed at the believers.
4:58–59 trusts; obey God, the messenger, and ulū l-amr

Render trusts. Judge with justice. Obey God and obey the messenger and those in authority among you. If you dispute in anything, refer it to God and the messenger if you believe in God and the Last Day.

Two-verb structure: aṭīʿū llāha wa-aṭīʿū l-rasūla wa-ulī l-amri minkum. Ulū l-amr share the obey-slot in this sentence but the dispute-referral goes to God and the messenger, not named as going to ulū l-amr. That grammatical difference is why later law splits over whether “those in authority” bind independently. Level 1 records both the shared obey and the narrower referral.

QB-0089: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with “submit to governing authorities” (Rom 13; 1 Pet 2:13) and with “obey those who rule over you” (Heb 13:17). Referral of disputes to God and the messenger is this text’s own court.
4:60–65 ṭāghūt as judge; they do not believe until they make you judge

People who claim to believe in both sendings want judgment from ṭāghūt. When told come to what God sent down and to the messenger, hypocrites turn away. After a disaster they swear they meant only good. Turn from them, admonish, speak to their souls. No messenger was sent except to be obeyed by God’s leave. If they had come to you after self-wrong, asked forgiveness, and the messenger asked for them, they would have found God tawwāb. Then the oath: they do not believe until they make you judge in their disputes, find no tightness from your decision, and submit fully.

4:65 is the strongest “the messenger’s judgment is a faith-condition” verse so far. It sits next to 4:59’s referral rule. Together they bind this community’s disputes to God-and-messenger rather than to ṭāghūt.
4:66–70 if We had written kill yourselves; companions of the prophets

If We had prescribed that they kill themselves or leave their homes, only a few would have done it. Whoever obeys God and the messenger is with those favored: prophets, ṣiddīqīn, shuhadāʾ, ṣāliḥīn — excellent companions. Bounty from God.
QB-0090: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with “cloud of witnesses” / being gathered to the faithful (Heb 11–12). The four-fold company is this verse’s own roster.
a portion of the Book — recurring
does not forgive that partners be associated
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on first-commandment gravity; NT unforgivable is a different file
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Rom 13 / Heb 13; referral is to God and the messenger
Portion of the Book; displace words; hear and disobey; ra'ina
Confirm what is with you before a sabbath-like curse
Shirk not forgiven; less than that for whom He wills
Jibt and taghut; envy of Abraham's house given Book and kingdom
Trusts; judge justly; obey God, messenger, and ulu l-amr; disputes to God and the messenger
They do not believe until they make you judge and submit fully
Obedient are with prophets, siddiqin, shuhada', salihin

The prior book is still “what is with you,” and words are still being displaced. Shirk is ranked as the unforgiven meeting-sin. Authority is God, then the messenger, then those in authority among you — with disputes sent back to the first two. Faith in this block includes accepting the messenger’s judgment without tightness of chest.
Next: 4:71–93 (fighting cluster, wronging one’s soul, the greeting, slaying one who offers peace, grades of sitting-back vs striving).

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP04 vv071-094
paragraphs: Note: Describes the text. Not a targeting guide.

O believers, take your precautions; advance in detachments or all together. Among you is one who lags; if a disaster hits you he says God has favored me that I was not with them; if bounty from God hits you he says as if there were no affection between you and him: would that I had been with them so I would have won a great win. Let those fight in God’s way who sell this world for the hereafter; whoever fights in God’s way and is killed or overcomes — We shall give him a great reward. What is with you that you do not fight in God’s way and for the mustaḍʿafīn of men, women, and children who say our Lord take us out of this town whose people are ẓālim; appoint for us from You a walī and a naṣīr? Those who believe fight in God’s way; those who disbelieve fight in ṭāghūt’s way. Fight the awliyāʾ of Satan; Satan’s plot is weak. Have you not seen those who were told restrain your hands, establish prayer, give zakāt — then when fighting was written on them a party feared people as God’s fear or a stronger fear, and said our Lord why did You write fighting on us? Would that You deferred us to a near term. Say the enjoyment of this world is little; the hereafter is better for the one who fears. Wherever you are, death will catch you even if you are in lofty towers. If good hits them they say this is from God; if evil hits them they say this is from you. Say all is from God. What is with these people that they scarcely understand a word? What hits you of good is from God; what hits you of evil is from yourself. We sent you to people as a messenger. Whoever obeys the messenger has obeyed God; whoever turns away — We did not send you as a keeper over them. They say obedience; when they go out from you a party of them plan by night other than what you say. So turn from them and rely on God. Do they not ponder the Quran? If it were from other than God they would have found in it much difference. When a matter of security or fear comes to them they broadcast it; if they had referred it to the messenger and to those in authority among them, those who extract it among them would have known it. If not for God’s bounty and mercy you would have followed Satan except a few. Fight in God’s way; you are not charged except for yourself. Urge the believers. God may restrain the might of those who disbelieve. Whoever intercedes a good intercession has a share of it; whoever intercedes an evil intercession has a share of it. When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it or return it. God — there is no god but He; He will gather you to the Day of Rising. What is with you regarding the hypocrites, two groups? God has thrown them back for what they earned. Do you want to guide whom God has sent astray? God has not made for you a way against them. They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. Do not take from them awliyāʾ until they emigrate in God’s way. If they turn back, take them and fight them wherever you find them; do not take from them walī or helper — except those who join a people between whom and you is a compact, or who come to you with their breasts constricted from fighting you or fighting their people. If God had willed He would have given them authority over you and they would have fought you. If they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, God has not made for you a way against them. You will find others who want to be secure from you and secure from their people; whenever they are returned to fitnah they are overturned in it. If they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands, take them and fight them wherever you find them. Those — We have made for you against them a clear slṭān. It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error. Whoever kills a believer by error: freeing a believing neck and blood-money delivered to his family unless they give it as ṣadaqa. If he was from a people at war with you and he was a believer: freeing a believing neck. If from a people between you and them a compact: blood-money and freeing a believing neck. Whoever does not find the means: fasting two consecutive months, a tawba from God. O believers, when you go forth in God’s way, tabayyanū — make clear — and do not say to one who offers you peace: you are not a believer, seeking the goods of this life. With God are many gains. You were like that before; God conferred favor on you, so make clear. God is aware of what you do.
This packet describes clauses. It is not an operational guide.
4:71–76 sitters vs fighters; oppressed in the town

Precautions; detachments or together. The lagger’s two speeches: disaster → God favored me; bounty → would that I had a share. Fight in God’s way those who sell this world for the hereafter; killed or victorious: great reward. Why do you not fight in God’s way and for the mustaḍʿafīn — men, women, and children — who ask to be taken out of a ẓālim town and given a walī and naṣīr? Believers fight in God’s way; disbelievers fight in ṭāghūt’s way. Satan’s plot is weak.
The oppressed-in-the-town clause is the stated why-fight in this block, next to the sell-the-world clause. Traditional asbāb: Meccan stay-behinds. Level 1 is the prayer of the weak in a ẓālim town.
4:77–79 from restrain-your-hands to fighting written; all is from God vs from yourself

Some were told restrain hands, pray, give zakāt; when fighting was written a party feared people as God’s fear. Why did You write fighting? Defer us. World-enjoyment is little. Death finds you in towers. Good they credit to God; evil they credit to you (the messenger). Say: all is from God. Then: good from God, evil from yourself. We sent you as a messenger. Obeying the messenger is obeying God; you are not a keeper over those who turn.

Two adjacent theodicy sentences: “all is from God” and “evil is from yourself.” Hold both. Night-planners vs what they say to his face. Ponder the Quran; if it were from other than God there would be much ikhtilāf. Security-or-fear news should go to the messenger and ulū l-amr, not be broadcast.
4:84–87 fight; you are charged only for yourself; greeting

Fight in God’s way; you are not charged except for yourself; urge the believers. God may restrain the disbelievers’ might. Good intercession / evil intercession each carry a share. Greeting: return with better or equal. God will gather to the Day of Rising. No god but He.

Hypocrites as two groups; God sent them back. Do not take them as awliyāʾ until they emigrate. If they turn back: fight them wherever found — except those who join a people with whom you have a compact, or who come with breasts constricted from fighting you or their people. If they withdraw, do not fight you, and offer peace: God has not made a way against them. Another type wants security from both sides and falls back into fitnah; if they do not withdraw and offer peace and restrain hands, a clear slṭān is named.
Level 1 contains both a pursue-clause and a peace-offered-no-way clause. Do not flatten one with the other. Compact-peoples are a third category.
4:92–94 error-killing; do not deny the greeting

A believer is not to kill a believer except by error. Error-kit: freeing a believing neck + blood-money to the family unless remitted; variants if the slain is from a hostile people or a compact-people; fasting two months if no means.
4:94: when you go forth, make clear. Do not say to one who offers you al-salām: you are not a believer — seeking the goods of this life. You were like that before; God favored you. Make clear.

QB-0091: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with cities-of-refuge / unintentional homicide (Num 35; Deut 19; Josh 20) — a neck-freeing plus blood-money kit instead of the refuge-city kit. 4:94 is an anti-spoils-misidentification rule: a greeting of peace is not to be overridden for worldly goods. Gospel analogue for greeting-return is thinner (Matt 5:47; 10:12–13); the specific “do not un-believe the greeter” is this verse’s own.
Error-killing kit; do not deny the peace-greeter
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Num 35 refuge logic; 4:94 is this text's own anti-spoils rule
Laggers; fight for the oppressed in a zalim town; believers vs taghut fighters
From restrain-hands to fighting written; all from God and evil from yourself
Obeying the messenger is obeying God; ponder the Quran; little difference-test
Charged only for yourself; greeting returned better or equal
Hypocrites; compact-people; if they offer peace God made no way against them
Error-killing: neck and blood-money; do not tell the greeter he is not a believer

Fighting in this block is tied to selling the world, to the weak in a ẓālim town, and to ṭāghūt’s fighters. Peace offered plus hands restrained closes a way. A greeting of peace is not to be cancelled for loot. Error-killing has a payment-and-freeing kit, not a refuge-city kit.
Next: 4:95–113 (sitters not equal to strivers; the one who wrongs himself; God forgives whom He wills; the secret consultation).

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP05 vv095-113
paragraphs: Not equal are the sitters of the believers — other than the harmed — and the mujāhidūn in God’s way with their property and their selves. God has preferred the mujāhidūn with their property and selves over the sitters by a degree. To each God has promised the good; God has preferred the mujāhidūn over the sitters with a great reward — degrees from Him, forgiveness, and mercy. Those the angels take while they are wronging themselves: in what condition were you? We were mustaḍʿafīn in the land. Was God’s earth not wide so you could emigrate in it? Those: refuge is Jahannam. Except the mustaḍʿafīn of men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan and are not guided to a way: God may pardon them. Whoever emigrates in God’s way will find in the earth many a refuge and amplitude. Whoever goes out from his house emigrating to God and His messenger, then death catches him: his reward has fallen on God. When you go forth in the land there is no blame on you that you shorten the prayer if you fear those who disbelieve may put you to trial. When you are among them and stand for them the prayer: a party stands with you and takes arms; when they have prostrated let them be behind you; let another party who have not prayed come and pray with you; let them take precaution and arms. Those who disbelieve wish you would neglect your arms and baggage so they could come down on you in one swoop. No blame if you are hurt by rain or ill to lay down arms; take your precaution. When you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting, and on your sides; when you are secure, establish the prayer. The prayer is on the believers a timed kitāb. Do not weaken in pursuit of the people; if you are hurting they hurt as you hurt, and you hope from God what they do not hope. We have sent down to you the Book with truth that you may judge between people by what God has shown you. Do not be an advocate for the treacherous. Ask God’s forgiveness. Do not argue for those who betray themselves; God does not love who is a treacherous sinner. They hide from people and do not hide from God; He is with them when they pass the night in speech He does not approve. Here you are, you argued for them in this life; who will argue with God for them on the Day of Rising? Whoever does evil or wrongs himself then asks God’s forgiveness will find God forgiving, merciful. Whoever earns a sin earns it only against himself. Whoever earns a fault or a sin then throws it on an innocent has taken on a slander and a clear sin. If not for God’s bounty on you and His mercy, a party of them would have resolved to mislead you. They mislead only themselves and they do not harm you at all. God sent down on you the Book and ḥikmah and taught you what you did not know. God’s bounty on you is great.

Not equal: qāʿidūn (except ḍarar) vs mujāhidūn with property and selves. Preference by a degree; then a great reward; then degrees, forgiveness, mercy. Both are promised al-ḥusnā. The exception for the harmed/disabled is Level 1. Jihād here is named as property-and-self in God’s way; do not collapse it only to battlefield without the verse’s own pair (amwāl / anfus).
4:97–100 angels at death; earth wide; death on the road

Angels take people who are ẓālimī anfusihim. Excuse: we were oppressed in the land. Reply: was God’s earth not wide enough to emigrate? Jahannam except the truly unable — men, women, children who cannot devise a way. God may pardon them. Whoever emigrates finds many a murāgham and amplitude. Whoever leaves his house emigrating to God and His messenger and death catches him: the reward has fallen on God.

This is the hard twin of 4:75’s oppressed-in-the-town prayer. 4:75 asked why you do not fight for them; 4:97 tells those who can leave that “we were oppressed” is not enough if the earth is wide. The unable are excepted.
QB-0092: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with exile-and-sojourn as faith-act (Abraham leaving; Heb 11:8–16 strangers and exiles). The angel-interrogation at death is this text’s own scene.

On the land, if you fear fitnah from those who disbelieve: no blame to shorten the prayer. When you stand with them: rotating two parties, arms held, prostration then switch. They wish you would neglect arms and baggage. Rain or illness: you may lay arms down; still take precaution. After prayer: remember God standing, sitting, on your sides (same triad as 3:191). When secure: establish the prayer. Prayer is on the believers a timed kitāb. Do not weaken in pursuit; they hurt as you hurt; you hope from God what they do not.
4:105–113 judge by what God showed you; do not plead the treacherous

Book sent down with truth so you may judge between people by what God showed you. Do not advocate for the khāʾinīn. Do not argue for those who betray themselves. They hide from people, not from God; He is with them in the night-speech He does not approve. Who will argue with God for them at the Rising? Whoever does evil or wrongs himself then asks forgiveness finds God ghafūr raḥīm. Sin is earned against the self. Casting it on an innocent is slander plus a clear sin. A party would have misled you; they mislead only themselves; they do not harm you. God sent down the Book and ḥikmah and taught you what you did not know.

Asbāb often name a theft blamed on a Jew to spare a Muslim (the Ṭuʿma / Bashīr reports). TRADITION for the names. Level 1 is: do not plead the self-betrayer; forgiveness is open after self-wrong; do not dump the sin on an innocent.
QB-0093: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with not perverting judgment for the powerful (Exod 23:1–3, 6–8; Deut 16:18–20; Isa 1:17). The night-counsel that God overhears is this scene’s own.
Emigrate; earth wide; death on the road
Do not plead the treacherous; do not dump sin on the innocent
Sitters not equal to strivers; disabled excepted; both promised good
Angels at death of those wronging themselves; earth was wide; unable excepted
Death while emigrating: reward has fallen on God
Shortened prayer and prayer of fear; prayer is a timed kitab
Judge by what God showed you; do not advocate the treacherous
Ask forgiveness after self-wrong; do not throw the sin on an innocent; Book and hikmah taught you

Strivers are preferred by degrees; sitters who are not disabled still have the promised good. “We were oppressed” does not cover those who could have left. Prayer can be shortened and rotated under fear; it remains a timed kitāb. Do not use the Book to plead a traitor or to hang an innocent.
Next: 4:114–126 (no good in most secret talk; shirk repeated as unforgiven; Abraham taken as friend) then 4:127–176 to close orphans-women-kalāla.

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP06 vv114-126
paragraphs: No good in much of their secret talk except who commands ṣadaqa or maʿrūf or iṣlāḥ between people. Whoever does that seeking God’s face, We shall give him a great reward. Whoever splits from the messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We turn him to what he has turned to and roast him in Jahannam. God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him; He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Whoever associates with God has gone far astray. They call besides Him only female beings; they call only a rebellious Satan. God cursed him. He said I will take of Your servants an appointed share; I will lead them astray, fill them with hopes, command them so they slit the ears of cattle, command them so they alter God’s creation. Whoever takes Satan as a walī besides God has lost a clear loss. He promises them and fills them with hopes; Satan promises them only ghurūr. Those: their refuge is Jahannam; they find no escape. Those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt We shall admit to Gardens. God’s promise is true; who is more truthful in speech than God? Not by your wishes nor the wishes of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil is repaid with it and will not find besides God a walī or naṣīr. Whoever does ṣāliḥāt — male or female — and is a believer: those enter the Garden and are not wronged a naqīr. Who is better in dīn than one who submits his face to God and is a muḥsin and follows the millah of Abraham ḥanīfan? God took Abraham as a khalīl. To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. God encompasses everything.
4:114–115 secret talk; splitting from the messenger

Most najwā has no good in it except ṣadaqa, maʿrūf, or repair between people, done seeking God’s face. Whoever separates from the messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than the believers’ way is turned to what he turned to. This is a post-clarity schism verse: the messenger plus the believers’ way as the named path.

Same sentence as 4:48: shirk not forgiven; less than that for whom He wills. They invoke ināth (female beings) and a rebellious Satan. God’s curse. Satan’s speech: an appointed share of the servants; lead astray; hopes; slit cattle-ears; alter God’s creation. Taking Satan as walī is clear loss. His promises are only delusion. Refuge Jahannam; no exit.

Altering God’s creation and ear-slitting sit in a Satan-program list, not as a separate legal code here. Later fiqh sometimes reads 4:119 onto tattooing, castration, or other body-alterations — Level 4. Level 1 is Satan claiming a share and a program of misguidance plus ritual-mutilation of livestock.
4:122–124 not by wishes; male and female

Believers who do ṣāliḥāt: Gardens. God’s promise is true. Not by your wishes and not by the wishes of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil is repaid with it. Whoever does ṣāliḥāt — male or female — and is a believer: Garden, not wronged a speck. Repeats the male-female work parity of 3:195. “Not by wishes” undercuts both this community’s and the Book-people’s confidence that affiliation alone settles the account.
Who is better in dīn than one who aslama wajhahu li-llāh, is a muḥsin, and follows Abraham’s millah ḥanīfan? God took Abraham as khalīl. Heavens and earth are God’s; He encompasses everything.

Khalīl is the title. QB-0094: AGREEMENT with Isa 41:8 / 2 Chr 20:7 / Jas 2:23 — Abraham as God’s friend. The Quran adds the title to the already-running ḥanīf-muslim file (2:135; 3:67). Submission of the face plus iḥsān plus Abraham’s millah is named as the better dīn, in the same surah as 4:48/116’s unforgiven shirk.
No good in most secret talk except sadaqa, ma'ruf, islah
Splitting from the messenger after clarity; other than the believers' way
Shirk unforgiven repeated; Satan's share, hopes, ear-slit, alter creation
Not by your wishes or the Book-people's; male and female believers who do salih
Better din: submit the face, ihsan, millah of Abraham; God took him as khalil

4:48’s sentence is repeated. Satan is given a speech and a program. Affiliation-wishes on both sides are set down. Abraham is named God’s friend. Next packet should take the orphan-women reprise and the last kalāla verse that closes the surah (4:127–176), split if needed at 4:152/153.

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP07 vv127-152
paragraphs: They ask you for a ruling about women. Say: God gives you a ruling about them and about what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them while you desire to marry them, and the oppressed among children, and that you stand for orphans with qisṭ. If a woman fears nushūz or iʿrāḍ from her husband, there is no blame on them that they make a ṣulḥ between them; ṣulḥ is better. Selves are present with greed. If you do good and fear, God is aware of what you do. You will not be able to be just among wives even if you are eager; do not incline all the incline and leave her as hanging. If you repair and fear, God is forgiving. If they separate, God will enrich each from His amplitude. To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. We have instructed those given the Book before you and you: fear God. If you disbelieve, to God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; God is sufficient as wakīl. If He wills He can put you away, O people, and bring others. Whoever wants the reward of this world: with God is the reward of this world and the hereafter. O believers, be qawwāmīn with qisṭ, witnesses for God, even if against yourselves or parents and kin. If he is rich or poor, God is worthier of both. Do not follow desire so you not be just. If you distort or turn away, God is aware. O believers, believe in God and His messenger and the Book He sent down on His messenger and the Book He sent down before. Whoever disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has gone far astray. Those who believe then disbelieve then believe then disbelieve then increase in kufr: God will not forgive them or guide them to a way. Give the hypocrites tidings of a painful punishment — those who take the disbelievers as awliyāʾ rather than the believers. Do they seek ʿizza with them? ʿIzza is God’s altogether. He has sent down on you in the Book that when you hear God’s signs being disbelieved and mocked, do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation, or you will be like them. God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Jahannam all together — those who wait upon you: if you have a fatḥ from God they say were we not with you, and if the disbelievers have a share they say did we not prevail upon you and protect you from the believers? God will judge between you on the Day of Rising. God has not made for the disbelievers a way over the believers. The hypocrites deceive God, and He deceives them. When they stand for prayer they stand lazy, showing off to people, not remembering God except a little, wavering between that, neither to these nor to those. Do not take the disbelievers as awliyāʾ rather than believers. Do you want to give God a clear slṭān against you? The hypocrites are in the lowest reach of the Fire; you will not find for them a helper — except those who repent, put things right, hold fast to God, and make their dīn sincere for God. Those are with the believers. God will give the believers a great reward. What would God do with your punishment if you are thankful and believe? Those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and want to distinguish between God and His messengers, saying we believe in some and disbelieve in some, and want to take a way in between — those are the true disbelievers. Those who believe in God and His messengers and do not distinguish between any of them: He will give them their rewards.
4:127–130 orphan women reprise; husband’s nushūz; you will not be just among wives

They ask a fatwā about women. God answers with what is already recited: orphan girls not given what is written for them while you want to marry them; oppressed children; stand for orphans with qisṭ. This points back at 4:3 and 4:11 without rewriting them.

If a woman fears nushūz or turning-away from her husband: no blame that they ṣulḥ. Ṣulḥ is better. Selves are attended by greed. You will not be able to ʿadl among wives even if eager; do not incline all the way and leave her hanging. If they separate, God will enrich each from His amplitude.
4:34 was nushūz feared from the wife. 4:128 is nushūz feared from the husband. Both sit in one surah. The inability-to-be-just-among-wives sentence is the brake next to 4:3’s four-cap.
4:135 stand with justice even against yourselves
Qawwāmīn bi-l-qisṭ, witnesses for God, even against yourselves or parents and kin. Rich or poor: God is worthier of both. Do not follow hawā. Distorting or turning away is seen.
QB-0095: AGREEMENT of type with HB witness-against-your-own-house ethics (Exod 23:1–3; Deut 16:19; Lev 19:15). One of the Quran’s clearest anti-nepotism lines.
4:136 believe the messenger’s Book and the Book sent before

Believe in God, His messenger, the Book sent down on His messenger, and the Book sent down before. Disbelief in God, angels, books, messengers, Last Day: far astray. The prior Book is again an object of required īmān, not a discarded file. Thickens QCA-0004 / QI-0003.
4:137–146 hypocrites: yo-yo īmān, lazy prayer, lowest Fire, except

Believe-disbelieve-believe-disbelieve-increase: no forgive, no way. Hypocrites take kāfir awliyāʾ. Do not sit with those who mock the signs until they change the talk (already 6:68 / 4:140). They wait on you: your fatḥ they claim to share; the other side’s share they claim to have shielded you. Prayer lazy, riyāʾ, little dhikr, mudhdhabdhabīn — neither these nor those. Lowest reach of the Fire; no helper — except who repent, repair, hold to God, and make dīn sincere. Those are with the believers.

Those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and want to separate God from His messengers — we believe in some and disbelieve in some — and want a way in between: those are the true kāfirūn. Those who believe in God and His messengers and do not distinguish between any of them: their rewards.

This is the Quran’s explicit ban on a pick-and-choose prophet list. It will sit immediately before 4:153–157’s Jesus/crucifixion panel. Level 1 here is the no-distinction rule, aimed in the first instance at those who accept some messengers and refuse this one (and, in the next block, at claims about Jesus).

QB-0096: CONTRAST with any Christian or Jewish ranking that receives some prophets and refuses later or parallel figures. PARTIAL AGREEMENT with “one God, many prophets” as a stated ideal; the membership of the list is the fight.
Witness even against yourselves and kin
AGREEMENT of type with Exod 23 / Deut 16 / Lev 19
Fatwa on women points back to orphan girls and qist
Wife fears husband's nushuz; sulh better; you will not be just among wives
Qawwamin with qist even against selves, parents, kin
Believe this Book and the Book sent before; yo-yo iman not forgiven
Hypocrites: mock-sessions, lazy prayer, lowest Fire, except sincere tawba
Wanting to separate God from His messengers is the true kufr; no distinction among them

The surah’s opening orphan-and-wives file is restated. Husband-nushūz has a ṣulḥ door. Justice binds even against your own house. The prior Book is still an object of īmān. Distinguishing among messengers is named as the real kufr. Next packet is the surah close: 4:153–176, including 4:157 (they did not kill him) and 4:171 (do not say three) and 4:176 (last kalāla).

packets.title: S004 Al-Nisa CP08 vv153-176
paragraphs: Crucifixion comparison note already on disk. This packet reads 4:157 in canonical place.

The People of the Book ask you to bring down on them a Book from heaven. They asked Moses for greater than that: show us God openly; the thunderbolt took them for their ẓulm. Then they took the calf after the clear signs; We pardoned that and gave Moses a clear slṭān. We raised the mount over them for their covenant; We said enter the gate in prostration; do not transgress the sabbath; We took from them a firm covenant. For their breaking the covenant, their kufr in God’s signs, their killing the prophets without right, their saying our hearts are wrapped — rather God sealed them for their kufr so they believe only a little — and for their kufr and their saying against Mary a great slander, and their saying we killed the Messiah Jesus son of Mary the messenger of God: they did not kill him and they did not crucify him but it was made to appear to them. Those who differ about it are in doubt; they have no knowledge except following ẓann; they did not kill him for certain. Rather God raised him to Himself. There is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death; on the Day of Rising he will be a witness against them. For ẓulm of those who were Jews We made unlawful good things that had been lawful, and for their barring much from God’s way, and their taking ribā when they were forbidden it, and their consuming people’s property by bāṭil. Those of them who are firm in knowledge and the believers believe in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you. The muqīmīn of the prayer, the givers of zakāt, the believers in God and the Last Day: We shall give them a great reward. We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon; We gave David the Zabūr. Messengers We have told you and messengers We have not told you; God spoke to Moses directly. Messengers as bringers of good news and warners so there would be no argument for people against God after the messengers. God bears witness that He sent down what He sent down; the angels bear witness; God is sufficient as witness. Those who disbelieve and bar from God’s way have gone far astray. Those who disbelieve and do ẓulm: God is not about to forgive them or guide them except the path of Jahannam. People, the messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord; believe, it is better for you. If you disbelieve, to God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. People of the Book, do not go beyond bounds in your dīn and do not say about God except the truth. The Messiah Jesus son of Mary is only a messenger of God and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. Believe in God and His messengers. Do not say three. Desist; it is better for you. God is only one God. Glory to Him that He should have a son. To Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, nor the angels brought near. Those who disdain His worship and are proud: He will gather them all. Those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt: He will pay them their wages in full and give more of His bounty. Those who disdain and are proud: He will punish them. People, a proof has come to you from your Lord; We have sent down to you a clear light. Those who believe in God and hold fast to Him: He will admit them to mercy and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path. They ask you for a ruling. Say God gives you a ruling about kalāla. If a man dies with no child and has a sister, she has half of what he leaves; he inherits her if she has no child. If there are two sisters, two-thirds. If they are brothers and sisters, the male has the like of the portion of two females. God makes clear to you lest you go astray. God is knowing of everything.
4:153–155 book from heaven; calf; mount; wrapped hearts

Demand: bring down a Book from heaven. Escalation memory: show us God openly; thunderbolt; calf after signs; pardon; mount raised; enter the gate prostrate; sabbath; firm covenant. Broken covenant, kufr in signs, killing prophets, qulūbunā ghulf — God sealed them; they believe only a little. Same wrapped-hearts line as 2:88.

A great slander against Mary is listed among the crimes. The Quran does not quote the slander. Tafsir usually hears the charge of unchastity. Level 1 is that a great slander was said. 19:27–28 will later stage a people accusing her; not yet in order.

The boast: we killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God. Denial: they did not kill him, did not crucify him; shubbiha lahum; differers are in doubt; no knowledge, only ẓann; they did not kill him yaqīnan. Bal rafaʿahu llāhu ilayhi. Then 4:159: every kitābī will believe in him before his death; he will be a witness against them at the Rising.

See Comparison_Quranic_Crucifixion_Views.docx for the reading-range. This packet does not close QB-0097–0100. It locates 4:157 after 4:150–152 (do not distinguish among messengers) and before 4:171 (do not say three). The denial is aimed at a boast attributed to those who said they killed him, inside a list of covenant-crimes, not as a free-standing treatise on Roman execution.

For ẓulm, good things that had been lawful were made unlawful; barring from the way; ribā after it was forbidden; consuming property by bāṭil. Then: the rāsikhūn in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you. Prayer-establishers, zakāt-givers, God-and-Last-Day believers: great reward. Remnant language again after 3:113 / 3:199 / 4:162.
4:163–170 same-channel revelation; David given the Zabūr; Moses spoken to

Revealed to you as to Noah and the prophets after him. Named: Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon; David given the Zabūr. Some messengers told, some not. God spoke to Moses taklīman. Messengers as bearers of news and warners so people have no ḥujja against God after them. God and the angels witness the sending-down. Messenger has come with truth; believe; if you disbelieve the heavens are still God’s.

QB-0101: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with a named prophet-list overlapping the HB (Noah through Solomon plus Jesus). Zabūr given to David maps onto Psalms as a received label, not a verse-by-verse identity claim.

People of the Book: do not go beyond bounds in your dīn; do not say about God except the truth. The Messiah Jesus son of Mary is only a messenger of God and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. Believe in God and His messengers. Do not say three. Desist. God is only one God. Glory that He should have a son. The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant, nor the angels brought near. The proud who disdain worship will be gathered.
Word + spirit + messenger in one sentence. 3:45 already had kalima. 4:171 adds rūḥ from Him and then immediately: do not say three; no son. Level 1 holds the titles and the ban together.

QB-0102: CONTRAST with Nicene / Gospel high Christology (John 1 Word; Matt 28 baptismal three; later Trinity). PARTIAL AGREEMENT that Jesus is a word and from God’s spirit in some Christian speech — then the Quran uses those words to block threeness and sonship. Do not pretend the shared nouns are shared doctrine.

A proof has come; a clear light sent down. Those who believe and hold fast: mercy, bounty, straight path. They ask a fatwā. Kalāla: no child, a sister takes half; he inherits her if she has no child; two sisters two-thirds; mixed siblings: male = two females. God makes clear lest you go astray.

4:12 already had a kalāla sixth / third. 4:176 is a second kalāla table focused on siblings when there is no child. Later law coordinates the two verses. Level 1: both exist. The surah that opened with orphan property closes on sibling shares.

Al-Nisāʾ opened with one nafs and the wombs, capped marriage at four with a justice-brake, gave daughters and widows named shares, set qiwāma next to two-family arbitration, ranked shirk as unforgiven, bound disputes to God and the messenger, denied the kill-the-Messiah boast, forbade saying three, and ended on kalāla. Jesus in this surah: word, spirit, messenger, not killed as they boasted, raised to God, witness, not a third of three, not a son.
Next canonical surah: S005 al-Māʾida. First packet 5:1–11 (contracts, hunting in iḥrām, food of the Book-people, food of the muḥṣanāt of the Book-people).
Prophet list + Zabur given to David
PARTIAL AGREEMENT of names with HB roster
Word and spirit, then do not say three
CONTRAST with Trinitarian use of Word; shared nouns not shared doctrine
Book-from-heaven demand; calf; mount; wrapped hearts
They did not kill him or crucify him; shubbiha; God raised him; kitabi will believe before his death
Good things made unlawful; riba; rasikhun among them believe both sendings
Same-channel revelation; David given the Zabur; Moses spoken to
Jesus: messenger, word cast to Mary, spirit from Him; do not say three; no son
Second kalala table: sister half; two sisters two-thirds; mixed male = two females

pickthall.name: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran

verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًۭا كَثِيرًۭا وَنِسَآءًۭ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًۭا
verses.itani: O people! Fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and propagated from them many men and women. And revere God whom you ask about, and the parents. Surely, God is Watchful over you.
verses.pickthall: O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate and from them twain hath spread abroad a multitude of men and women. Be careful of your duty toward Allah in Whom ye claim (your rights) of one another, and toward the wombs (that bare you). Lo! Allah hath been a watcher over you.

verses.arabic: وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰٓ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا۟ ٱلْخَبِيثَ بِٱلطَّيِّبِ ۖ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوٓا۟ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ إِلَىٰٓ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حُوبًۭا كَبِيرًۭا
verses.itani: And give orphans their properties, and do not substitute the bad for the good. And do not consume their properties by combining them with yours, for that would be a serious sin.
verses.pickthall: Give unto orphans their wealth. Exchange not the good for the bad (in your management thereof) nor absorb their wealth into your own wealth. Lo! that would be a great sin.

verses.arabic: وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا۟ فِى ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُوا۟ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَ ۖ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ فَوَٰحِدَةً أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعُولُوا۟
verses.itani: If you fear you cannot act fairly towards the orphans—then marry the women you like—two, or three, or four. But if you fear you will not be fair, then one, or what you already have. That makes it more likely that you avoid bias.
verses.pickthall: And if ye fear that ye will not deal fairly by the orphans, marry of the women, who seem good to you, two or three or four; and if ye fear that ye cannot do justice (to so many) then one (only) or (the captives) that your right hands possess. Thus it is more likely that ye will not do injustice.

verses.arabic: وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَٰتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةًۭ ۚ فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ نَفْسًۭا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـًۭٔا مَّرِيٓـًۭٔا
verses.itani: Give women their dowries graciously. But if they willingly forego some of it, then consume it with enjoyment and pleasure.
verses.pickthall: And give unto the women (whom ye marry) free gift of their marriage portions; but if they of their own accord remit unto you a part thereof, then ye are welcome to absorb it (in your wealth).

verses.arabic: وَلَا تُؤْتُوا۟ ٱلسُّفَهَآءَ أَمْوَٰلَكُمُ ٱلَّتِى جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَٰمًۭا وَٱرْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا وَٱكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا۟ لَهُمْ قَوْلًۭا مَّعْرُوفًۭا
verses.itani: Do not give the immature your money which God has assigned to you for support. But provide for them from it, and clothe them, and speak to them with kind words.
verses.pickthall: Give not unto the foolish (what is in) your (keeping of their) wealth, which Allah hath given you to maintain; but feed and clothe them from it, and speak kindly unto them.

verses.arabic: وَٱبْتَلُوا۟ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُوا۟ ٱلنِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ ءَانَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًۭا فَٱدْفَعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَآ إِسْرَافًۭا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكْبَرُوا۟ ۚ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيًّۭا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرًۭا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًۭا
verses.itani: Test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage. If you find them to be mature enough, hand over their properties to them. And do not consume it extravagantly or hastily before they grow up. The rich shall not charge any wage, but the poor may charge fairly. When you hand over their properties to them, have it witnessed for them. God suffices as a Reckoner.
verses.pickthall: Prove orphans till they reach the marriageable age; then, if ye find them of sound judgment, deliver over unto them their fortune; and devour it not by squandering and in haste lest they should grow up Whoso (of the guardians) is rich, let him abstain generously (from taking of the property of orphans); and whoso is poor let him take thereof in reason (for his guardianship). And when ye deliver up their fortune unto orphans, have (the transaction) witnessed in their presence. Allah sufficeth as a Reckoner.

verses.arabic: لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌۭ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٌۭ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ ۚ نَصِيبًۭا مَّفْرُوضًۭا
verses.itani: Men receive a share of what their parents and relatives leave, and women receive a share of what their parents and relatives leave; be it little or much—a legal share.
verses.pickthall: Unto the men (of a family) belongeth a share of that which parents and near kindred leave, and unto the women a share of that which parents and near kindred leave, whether it be little or much - a legal share.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلْقِسْمَةَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينُ فَٱرْزُقُوهُم مِّنْهُ وَقُولُوا۟ لَهُمْ قَوْلًۭا مَّعْرُوفًۭا
verses.itani: If the distribution is attended by the relatives, and the orphans, and the needy, give them something out of it, and speak to them kindly.
verses.pickthall: And when kinsfolk and orphans and the needy are present at the division (of the heritage), bestow on them therefrom and speak kindly unto them.

verses.arabic: وَلْيَخْشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا۟ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةًۭ ضِعَٰفًا خَافُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًۭا سَدِيدًا
verses.itani: Those who are concerned about the fate of their weak children, in case they leave them behind, should fear God, and speak appropriate words.
verses.pickthall: And let those fear (in their behaviour toward orphans) who if they left behind them weak offspring would be afraid for them. So let them mind their duty to Allah, and speak justly.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِى بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًۭا ۖ وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًۭا
verses.itani: Those who consume the wealth of orphans illicitly consume only fire into their bellies; and they will roast in a Blaze.
verses.pickthall: Lo! Those who devour the wealth of orphans wrongfully, they do but swallow fire into their bellies, and they will be exposed to burning flame.

verses.arabic: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَوْلَٰدِكُمْ ۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلْأُنثَيَيْنِ ۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءًۭ فَوْقَ ٱثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ ۖ وَإِن كَانَتْ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصْفُ ۚ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدٌۭ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخْوَةٌۭ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصِى بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ ۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَآؤُكُمْ لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًۭا ۚ فَرِيضَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًۭا
verses.itani: God instructs you regarding your children: The male receives the equivalent of the share of two females. If they are daughters, more than two, they get two-thirds of what he leaves. If there is only one, she gets one-half. As for the parents, each gets one-sixth of what he leaves, if he had children. If he had no children, and his parents inherit from him, his mother gets one-third. If he has siblings, his mother gets one-sixth. After fulfilling any bequest and paying off debts. Your parents and your children—you do not know which are closer to you in welfare. This is God's Law. God is Knowing and Judicious.
verses.pickthall: Allah chargeth you concerning (the provision for) your children: to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and if there be women more than two, then theirs is two-thirds of the inheritance, and if there be one (only) then the half. And to each of his parents a sixth of the inheritance, if he have a son; and if he have no son and his parents are his heirs, then to his mother appertaineth the third; and if he have brethren, then to his mother appertaineth the sixth, after any legacy he may have bequeathed, or debt (hath been paid). Your parents and your children: Ye know not which of them is nearer unto you in usefulness. It is an injunction from Allah. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise.

verses.arabic: ۞ وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَٰجُكُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّهُنَّ وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌۭ فَلَكُمُ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍۢ ۚ وَلَهُنَّ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّكُمْ وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌۭ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم ۚ مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍۢ ۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌۭ يُورَثُ كَلَٰلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌۭ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌۭ فَلِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ ۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّۢ ۚ وَصِيَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: You get one-half of what your wives leave behind, if they had no children. If they had children, you get one-fourth of what they leave. After fulfilling any bequest and paying off debts. They get one-fourth of what you leave behind, if you have no children. If you have children, they get one-eighth of what you leave. After fulfilling any bequest and paying off debts. If a man or woman leaves neither parents nor children, but has a brother or sister, each of them gets one-sixth. If there are more siblings, they share one-third. After fulfilling any bequest and paying off debts, without any prejudice. This is a will from God. God is Knowing and Clement.
verses.pickthall: And unto you belongeth a half of that which your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child then unto you the fourth of that which they leave, after any legacy they may have bequeathed, or debt (they may have contracted, hath been paid). And unto them belongeth the fourth of that which ye leave if ye have no child, but if ye have a child then the eighth of that which ye leave, after any legacy ye may have bequeathed, or debt (ye may have contracted, hath been paid). And if a man or a woman have a distant heir (having left neither parent nor child), and he (or she) have a brother or a sister (only on the mother's side) then to each of them twain (the brother and the sister) the sixth, and if they be more than two, then they shall be sharers in the third, after any legacy that may have been bequeathed or debt (contracted) not injuring (the heirs by willing away more than a third of the heritage) hath been paid. A commandment from Allah. Allah is Knower, Indulgent.

verses.arabic: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
verses.itani: These are the bounds set by God. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger, He will admit him into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. That is the great attainment.
verses.pickthall: These are the limits (imposed by) Allah. Whoso obeyeth Allah and His messenger, He will make him enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow, where such will dwell for ever. That will be the great success.

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَعْصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُۥ يُدْخِلْهُ نَارًا خَٰلِدًۭا فِيهَا وَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌۭ مُّهِينٌۭ
verses.itani: But whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, and oversteps His bounds, He will admit him into a Fire, wherein he abides forever, and he will have a shameful punishment.
